audit.why: Nasus is helpless early and unbeatable late; Aatrox owning stages 1-5 and losing the last two matches the 48.34% win rate over 2,416 games.
audit.corrected: Kept; the timings that make it playable were added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late-game spike described Fury of the Sands only as making him "near-unkillable".
audit.why: Riot's text is more specific and more useful: it grants health, ATTACK RANGE, resists, and a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown. The extra range is why disengaging from an ulted Nasus fails, and the Q cooldown reduction is why his stacks land twice as often inside R.
audit.corrected: late now states what Fury of the Sands actually grants.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wither was described only as a slow, with no cooldown and no statement of what it actually blunts.
audit.why: Riot's text: Wither 'ages an enemy champion, decelerating their Move Speed and Attack Speed over time' on 15/14/13/12/11s. It ramps, and it cuts ATTACK SPEED as well as movement — which is why an Aatrox who opens a trade into a fresh Wither loses both his chase and his auto-weaves, and why opening after it is spent is the whole sequencing rule. Siphoning Strike (Q) itself reaches 3.5s at rank 5, so a stacked Nasus gets his empowered hit roughly twice as often as an unstacked one.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1] now name the 15s cooldown and tie the trade opening to it.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown-sequencing advice existed anywhere (flagged in packet defects).
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s and is the only thing that blunts your combo. Opening your trade in the window after it is spent is the single concrete sequencing rule in this lane.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid, wants.you[1] and wants.foe[1] now all carry the 15s and the "trade after Wither" rule.

edits.before: World Ender lets you commit hard trades through his W Wither slow; pop R, dash with E, and force him off the wave so he can't farm stacks safely.
edits.after: World Ender lets you commit through Wither (W, 15s at rank 1); pop R, dash with E, and force him off the wave so he can't farm stacks safely.

edits.before: Levels 2 through 6 all favor you and this is where you win or lose the whole matchup. With your Q pattern plus E you out-trade and out-drain him constantly — land the Q3 sweetspot, dash in with E, and force him off the wave so he can't stack. His W Wither will slow your attack speed and movement to blunt your combo, but World Ender's heal-amp and combat stats let you commit through it. Zone him hard: every denied stack and every missed CS is scaling you're stealing from his late game.
edits.after: Levels 2 through 6 all favour you and this is where you win or lose the whole matchup. With your Q pattern plus E you out-trade and out-drain him constantly — land the Q3 sweetspot, dash in with E, and force him off the wave so he can't stack. Wither (W) is 15s at rank 1 and slows your attack speed and movement to blunt the combo, so open your trade the moment it is spent; World Ender's heal-amp lets you commit through it anyway. Every denied stack is scaling stolen.

edits.before: The final phase belongs to Nasus, full stop. Once he reaches hundreds of Q stacks plus Spirit Fire and tank items, his empowered auto shreds you, his sustain out-heals your drain, and his R Fury of the Sands makes him a near-unkillable brawler. Grievous helps against his lifesteal but won't save a duel against a fully-stacked Nasus. Your only insurance is the lead you built early — end the game or keep him perpetually behind, because if he scales, you lose the 1v1.
edits.after: The final phase belongs to Nasus, full stop. Once he reaches hundreds of Q stacks plus Spirit Fire and tank items, his empowered auto shreds you, his Soul Eater lifesteal out-heals your drain, and Fury of the Sands (R) gives him health, attack range, resists and a shorter Siphoning Strike cooldown. Grievous helps against the lifesteal but won't save a duel against a stacked Nasus. Your insurance is the early lead — end it.
